thread:
Devon: paging — multiple regions seeing small % of traffic routed to wrong region, noticed by health-proxies. errors up ~1.8% and tail latency on POST /v1/generate spiking for a subset of customers. tagging oncall. :rotating_light:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: PD-INC-4728 assigned to Sara (oncall) — high error rate across cross-region routing.
Sara (oncall): I'm on it, grabbing runbook. anyone seeing DNS chatter or route churn?
Raj: seeing a steady stream of queries hitting us-west-2 that should be pinned to eu-west-1. pattern looks like 'pin:region' tag ignored for ~6% of requests.
Katie: confirmed for some customers with reserved-dedicated — stickiness lost for a subset of session ids. routing-policy logs show policy evaluation falling back to 'latency-steer' unexpectedly.
Devon: can we snapshot the policy decision path? Raj, can you grab a sample trace from the router?
Raj: grabbing. here's a sample decision log for request id 7f9a3:
```
policy_eval: start
rule: pin_check -> matched false
rule: latency_steer -> selected us-west-2
context: client_pref=eu-west-1, pinned_region=eu-west-1
notes: pinned_region header present but ignored
```

Sara (oncall): hmm pinned_region header present but the evaluator says matched false. Could be a header-parsing change or a recent policy release. Who rolled the policy?
Katie: we deployed a policy ABI change earlier this morning to short-circuit some legacy checks. rollout was gradual but looks like the new evaluator has a bug: header key name mismatch (`x-region-pin` vs `x-pin-region`). fallback path triggers latency_steer.
Devon: ok that explains it. impact estimate? which customer cohorts are affected?
Raj: mostly eu and apac customers with dedicated pool. Rough numbers: ~6% of traffic misrouted, 0.9% increase in 95th latency for eu customers, error rate bump up to 2% for those flows. No total outage.
Sara (oncall): escalate to networking and policy owner. @Networking Team please standby to push a hotfix. I'll page CS for impacted customers and mark SEV-3 for now.
pagerduty: Escalation: PD-INC-4728 -> Eng-SRE oncall. Severity: seV-3.
Networking Team: standing by. If it's a policy ABI mismatch we can roll the policy back in control-plane. Which environments affected? prod-only?
Katie: only prod control-plane rollout had the new evaluator. Canary didn't catch it because canary traffic didn't include the deprecated header variant.
Devon: mitigation plan: 1) rollback policy evaluator to previous version 2) temporarily bump header compatibility to accept both names 3) clear affected route cache 4) notify customers. Who can rollback now?
Raj: I can rollback the policy bundle. Running rollback command now:
```
rbctl policy rollback --bundle=policy-eval-v2 --to=policy-eval-v1 --env=prod
```
Devon: after rollback, let's invalidate route caches for pinned flows. Use the drain command for pinned buckets for eu-west-1.
```
routeshift invalidate --region=eu-west-1 --tag=pinned --mode=soft
```
Katie: rollback completed at control-plane. policy-eval-v1 restored. Confirming policy-eval logs now accept `x-region-pin` header.
Raj: starting cache invalidation. will monitor for error rate and misrouted traffic.
Sara (oncall): I'm opening a short customer advisory draft. Quick note: "We observed a small fraction of requests being routed to different regions due to a policy evaluator regression. We rolled back the change and we are monitoring. No data exposure." Thoughts?
Devon: add ETA for full verification — 60 minutes, watch three windows: 5m error rate, 1m p50/p95 latency, and routing-sticky samples.
Katie: metrics show misroute rate dropping after rollback. now at ~0.3% and trending down. p95 for eu customers back to baseline.
Raj: verifying traces show pinned_region respected again. sample trace for same id now:
```
policy_eval: start
rule: pin_check -> matched true
selected_region: eu-west-1
```
Networking Team: no further network-level action required. root cause tracked to policy evaluator header mismatch introduced in v2.
Sara (oncall): declaring incident status: mitigation in progress, impact reduced, continuing to monitor. paging noise -> reduce frequency. assigning postmortem to Katie+Raj+Devon.
Devon: postmortem action items: 1) tighten canary to include pinned header variants, 2) add unit/regression test for header aliasing, 3) improve deployment rollback runbook steps and add automated guard that alarms if pin mismatch rate > 0.5% for 10m.
Katie: will take the postmortem. I'll draft and include timeline + diffs. Also will add a temporary compatibility layer in evaluator to accept both headers for 2 weeks.
Sara (oncall): customer comms ready, sending to CS. I'll update incident channel after 60m verification. good work team. :thumbsup:
